questionText: [Set 43.1] In management theory, 'Efficiency' differs from 'Effectiveness' in that efficiency primarily focuses on:

options.text: Completing activities on time regardless of operational costs
Doing the task correctly with minimum cost and resource wastage
Establishing long-term strategic mission statements
Exercising authoritative disciplinary punishment on workers

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Bst (Nature and Significance of Management - Effectiveness vs Efficiency):
Effectiveness is about doing the right things, completing activities, and achieving goals on time. Efficiency is about doing things right, conducting operations with minimum resources, avoiding waste, and minimizing costs.

Hence, Option (B) is the correct answer.

solution.concept: Nature and Significance of Management: Effectiveness vs Efficiency
solution.detailed:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Bst (Nature and Significance of Management - Effectiveness vs Efficiency):
Effectiveness is about doing the right things, completing activities, and achieving goals on time. Efficiency is about doing things right, conducting operations with minimum resources, avoiding waste, and minimizing costs.

Hence, Option (B) is the correct answer.

keyConcept: Nature and Significance of Management: Effectiveness vs Efficiency

questionText: [Set 43.2] Henri Fayol's principle of 'Unity of Command' asserts that:

options.text: All departments should be unified under a single product manager
An individual employee should receive orders from and be accountable to only one superior
Wages should be strictly unified across all manufacturing plants
Authority and responsibility must be held by the board of directors exclusively

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Bst (Principles of Management - Fayol's Unity of Command):
Unity of command prevents dual subordination: each worker must receive instructions from only one boss. Dual subordination creates confusion, undermines discipline, causes overlapping duties, and creates interpersonal conflict.

Hence, Option (B) is the correct answer.

solution.concept: Principles of Management: Fayol's Unity of Command
solution.detailed:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Bst (Principles of Management - Fayol's Unity of Command):
Unity of command prevents dual subordination: each worker must receive instructions from only one boss. Dual subordination creates confusion, undermines discipline, causes overlapping duties, and creates interpersonal conflict.

Hence, Option (B) is the correct answer.

keyConcept: Principles of Management: Fayol's Unity of Command

questionText: [Set 43.3] Under F.W. Taylor's concept of Functional Foremanship, which specialist foreperson is responsible for keeping machines, tools, and equipment clean and in working order?

options.text: Gang Boss
Speed Boss
Repair Boss
Inspector

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Bst (Principles of Management - Taylor's Functional Foremanship):
Under the planning in-charge: Instruction Card Clerk, Route Clerk, Time and Cost Clerk, Disciplinarian. Under execution: Gang Boss (sets up tools), Speed Boss (maintains work tempo), Repair Boss (maintains machines/tools), Inspector (checks output quality).

Hence, Option (C) is the correct answer.

solution.concept: Principles of Management: Taylor's Functional Foremanship
solution.detailed:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Bst (Principles of Management - Taylor's Functional Foremanship):
Under the planning in-charge: Instruction Card Clerk, Route Clerk, Time and Cost Clerk, Disciplinarian. Under execution: Gang Boss (sets up tools), Speed Boss (maintains work tempo), Repair Boss (maintains machines/tools), Inspector (checks output quality).

Hence, Option (C) is the correct answer.

keyConcept: Principles of Management: Taylor's Functional Foremanship

questionText: [Set 43.4] The major economic and regulatory objectives of the Demonetisation initiative launched by the Government of India in November 2016 included:

options.text: Curtailing black money, curbing counterfeit currency, and promoting formal digital transactions
Abolishing all private banking institutions nationwide
Enforcing a fixed foreign exchange peg with the US dollar
Nationalising corporate retail conglomerates

detailedSolution:

Hence, Option (A) is the correct answer.

questionText: [Set 43.5] Which of the following is an inherent limitation of the planning function in modern dynamic business environments?

options.text: Planning leads to rigidity and may not work effectively in a turbulent, fast-changing environment
Planning eliminates all financial and operational risks automatically
Planning replaces the need for managerial coordination
Planning guarantees 100% commercial success for every new product launch

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Bst (Planning - Planning Premises and Limitations):
Limitations of planning include: (1) Planning leads to rigidity, (2) Planning may not work in a dynamic environment, (3) It reduces individual creativity, (4) It involves huge costs and time consumption, (5) It does not guarantee success.

Hence, Option (A) is the correct answer.

Detailed Solution:

Hence, Option (A) is the correct answer.

questionText: [Set 43.6] 'Span of Management' (or Span of Control) in organizational design refers to:

options.text: The geographic radius covered by a regional sales distribution office
The total tenure of an executive on the corporate board
The total capital budget allocated across operating subsidiaries
The number of subordinates that can be effectively managed and supervised by a superior

Span of management refers to the number of subordinates who report directly to a manager. It determines the levels of hierarchy and the shape (tall vs flat) of the organizational structure.

Hence, Option (D) is the correct answer.

questionText: [Set 43.7] Vestibule training is an off-the-job training method where trainees:

options.text: Learn on the actual equipment and machinery in a simulated classroom away from the shop floor
Work under the direct guidance of a master craftsman on the live assembly line
Are rotated across various organizational departments every month
Attend university evening lectures on corporate business ethics

detailedSolution:

Vestibule training uses duplicate equipment and machinery in a simulated workshop environment away from the production floor, allowing workers to master operations without risking accidents or interrupting live production.

Hence, Option (A) is the correct answer.

questionText: [Set 43.8] In Abraham Maslow's Need Hierarchy Theory of motivation, which of the following needs is placed at the highest level of psychological hierarchy?

options.text: Esteem needs
Social / Belongingness needs
Self-actualization needs
Safety and security needs

detailedSolution:

Hence, Option (C) is the correct answer.

questionText: [Set 43.9] The principle of 'Management by Exception' (MBE) in organizational control dictates that:

options.text: Only significant deviations that go beyond permissible tolerance limits should be brought to management's attention
Managers must inspect 100% of manufactured units individually
Exceptional workers should be exempted from organizational rules
Every minor minor deviation must be resolved by the CEO personally

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Bst (Controlling - Management by Exception (MBE)):
Management by exception is an important control principle stating that an attempt to control everything results in controlling nothing. Only critical deviations beyond established tolerance limits require senior managerial intervention.

Hence, Option (A) is the correct answer.

solution.detailed:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Bst (Controlling - Management by Exception (MBE)):
Management by exception is an important control principle stating that an attempt to control everything results in controlling nothing. Only critical deviations beyond established tolerance limits require senior managerial intervention.

Hence, Option (A) is the correct answer.

questionText: [Set 43.10] A company uses 'Trading on Equity' (favourable financial leverage) to increase its Return on Equity (ROE) when:

options.text: Return on Investment (ROI) is less than the interest rate on debentures
Return on Investment (ROI) is greater than the cost of borrowed debt capital
The company has zero debt and is funded 100% by equity shares
The corporate income tax rate is reduced to zero percent

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Bst (Financial Management - Trading on Equity (Financial Leverage)):
Trading on equity refers to the use of fixed-cost debt in the capital structure. If ROI > Cost of Debt, the excess earnings generated by borrowed funds accrue entirely to equity shareholders, increasing Earnings Per Share (EPS).

Hence, Option (B) is the correct answer.

solution.concept: Financial Management: Trading on Equity (Financial Leverage)
solution.detailed:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Bst (Financial Management - Trading on Equity (Financial Leverage)):
Trading on equity refers to the use of fixed-cost debt in the capital structure. If ROI > Cost of Debt, the excess earnings generated by borrowed funds accrue entirely to equity shareholders, increasing Earnings Per Share (EPS).

Hence, Option (B) is the correct answer.

keyConcept: Financial Management: Trading on Equity (Financial Leverage)

questionText: [Set 43.11] Treasury Bills (T-Bills) issued by the Reserve Bank of India on behalf of the Central Government are:

options.text: Interest-bearing perpetual debentures issued at a premium
Zero-coupon bonds issued at a discount and redeemed at par (minimum denomination Rs. 25,000)
Equity instruments tradeable exclusively on international commodity bourses
Commercial paper issued by blue-chip private manufacturing corporations

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Bst (Financial Markets - Treasury Bills (T-Bills) Characteristics):
Treasury bills are short-term promissory notes issued by the RBI to meet short-term government funding needs. Known as zero-coupon bonds, they pay no stated interest but are issued at a discount and redeemed at nominal par value.

Hence, Option (B) is the correct answer.

solution.detailed:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Bst (Financial Markets - Treasury Bills (T-Bills) Characteristics):
Treasury bills are short-term promissory notes issued by the RBI to meet short-term government funding needs. Known as zero-coupon bonds, they pay no stated interest but are issued at a discount and redeemed at nominal par value.

Hence, Option (B) is the correct answer.

questionText: [Set 43.12] The traditional Marketing Mix introduced by E. Jerome McCarthy comprises which four fundamental controllable variables?

options.text: Product, Price, Place, and Promotion
Production, Planning, Personnel, and Profit
Packaging, Positioning, Publicity, and People
Procurement, Processing, Policing, and Pricing

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Bst (Marketing - Marketing Mix Elements (4 Ps)):
The marketing mix is the combination of four controllable variables that a company blends to produce the response it wants in the target market: Product, Price, Place (distribution), and Promotion.

Hence, Option (A) is the correct answer.

solution.detailed:
Detailed Solution:

The marketing mix is the combination of four controllable variables that a company blends to produce the response it wants in the target market: Product, Price, Place (distribution), and Promotion.

Hence, Option (A) is the correct answer.

questionText: [Set 43.13] Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (District Commission) has pecuniary jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of goods or services paid as consideration does not exceed:

options.text: Rs. 10 Crores
Rs. 20 Lakhs
Rs. 50 Lakhs (per amended 2021 jurisdictional notifications)
Rs. 100 Crores

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Bst (Consumer Protection - Consumer Protection Act 2019 Pecuniary Jurisdiction):
Under the Consumer Protection Act 2019 (as amended by 2021 notifications): District Commission handles claims up to Rs. 50 lakhs; State Commission from Rs. 50 lakhs to Rs. 2 crores; National Commission for claims exceeding Rs. 2 crores.

Hence, Option (C) is the correct answer.

solution.concept: Consumer Protection: Consumer Protection Act 2019 Pecuniary Jurisdiction

Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Bst (Consumer Protection - Consumer Protection Act 2019 Pecuniary Jurisdiction):

Hence, Option (C) is the correct answer.

keyConcept: Consumer Protection: Consumer Protection Act 2019 Pecuniary Jurisdiction

questionText: [Set 43.36] A company uses 'Trading on Equity' (favourable financial leverage) to increase its Return on Equity (ROE) when:

options.text: Return on Investment (ROI) is less than the interest rate on debentures
The company has zero debt and is funded 100% by equity shares
The corporate income tax rate is reduced to zero percent
Return on Investment (ROI) is greater than the cost of borrowed debt capital

detailedSolution:

Hence, Option (D) is the correct answer.

questionText: [Set 43.37] Treasury Bills (T-Bills) issued by the Reserve Bank of India on behalf of the Central Government are:

options.text: Interest-bearing perpetual debentures issued at a premium
Zero-coupon bonds issued at a discount and redeemed at par (minimum denomination Rs. 25,000)
Equity instruments tradeable exclusively on international commodity bourses
Commercial paper issued by blue-chip private manufacturing corporations

detailedSolution:

questionText: [Set 43.40] In management theory, 'Efficiency' differs from 'Effectiveness' in that efficiency primarily focuses on:

options.text: Completing activities on time regardless of operational costs

Exercising authoritative disciplinary punishment on workers
Doing the task correctly with minimum cost and resource wastage
